subject: Reseed/checkpointing approach + rerank validation plan for Brightline migration
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Trent <alyssa@brightline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reseed/checkpointing approach + rerank validation plan for Brightline migration

Hi Alyssa —

Following our kickoff, attached is a concise operational proposal for the embedding + rerank migration. High level recommendation: do a hybrid seeding strategy (fast recent seed + background full backfill) and run a staged rerank validation before cutover. Attachments: seed_manifest_v1.csv (seed priority buckets), backfill-runbook.pdf (ops steps), rerank-testset-sample.csv (sample queries).

Summary (short):
- Seed policy: hydrate most-active 90 days first (fast path).
- Background backfill: full historical backfill at reduced concurrency, bucketed by content age, with checkpointed resumes and per-bucket verification checksums.
- Vector DB: target production Pinecone (dense index + vector metadata); dev/staging fallback to pgvector to keep costs low during canary.
- Throttling: limit to 300 concurrent chunk writes per region; apply jitter and exponential backoff on 429/5xx.
- Acceptance for rerank: offline A/B with holdout (2k queries), human label sample (200 queries), success criteria: NDCG@10 >= baseline + 0.06 OR MRR >= baseline + 0.08, and p95 latency impact <= +30ms.
- Rollout: staging canary -> 10% prod -> 50% -> full with automatic rollback on quality regression.

Operational notes (ops-critical):
- Each backfill run creates checkpoints every 10k documents; checkpoints uploaded to S3 and referenced in the runbook.
- We will ship a short smoke test that validates vector counts, top-3 similarity sanity, and rerank stability before enabling read traffic.
- Data handling: we will respect your retention flags and PII filters; manifest includes an explicit pii_exclude tag.

Ask: can you confirm the preferred maintenance window (we've penciled in the weekend of Jun 20-22), and whether you want the staging canary on your existing staging cluster or a temporary environment we spin up?

If this looks good I’ll create a Mutual Action Plan (MAP) with owners and dates and loop in Engineering for the backfill runner config.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
camila@redwood.ai

Attachments: seed_manifest_v1.csv (csv), backfill-runbook.pdf (pdf), rerank-testset-sample.csv (csv)
From: Alyssa Trent <alyssa@brightline.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>
Cc: Brightline Platform <eng+prod@brightline.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 12:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reseed/checkpointing approach + rerank validation plan for Brightline migration

Thanks Camila — this is very thorough. A couple immediate questions before we sign off on the MAP: 

1) Data privacy / PII: does the seed manifest remove or redact PII by default? We have customer emails and order IDs that cannot leave the Brightline environment unmasked. Do you have a standard PII filter we can run upstream?
2) SOC2 evidence: can you attach a short SOC2 summary (we'll need to hand to procurement)?
3) Canary environment: staging is shared across multiple teams — we'd prefer a temporary isolated canary if Redwood can stand it up (we can give credentials).
4) Maintenance window: our platform team suggested the weekend you proposed, but they asked whether we can limit write-heavy backfill to the low-traffic hours (02:00–06:00 local) and avoid peak index rebuilds on June 21.

Also — can you confirm whether Pinecone metadata supports our document-level visibility tags (we need to exclude certain internal docs from search results)?

Appreciate the plan, happy to sync on a short call if needed.

— Alyssa
Alyssa Trent
Head of Search + Relevance, Brightline
alyssa@brightline.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 16:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reseed/checkpointing approach + rerank validation plan for Brightline migration

Looping in our onboarding checklist and owners here. Camila — great draft. I propose we convert this into a short Mutual Action Plan (MAP) and set owners:

- Camila (SEA): runbook + seed manifest verification by 2025-06-13
- Naomi (Eng) : backfill runner config + checkpoint tests by 2025-06-16
- Monica (CS): holdout query list + human label coordination by 2025-06-15
- Marissa (CS Lead): business acceptance and rollout approval (timeline windows) by 2025-06-18

Immediate next steps I will own with Camila: export a 2k holdout set for offline rerank eval and a 200-sample labeling sheet for Brightline raters. Monica — once you have labeling capacity, please confirm tooling (DocuSign? we use Prolific for quick label runs, but Brightline may have an internal annotation team).

I’ll also add the HubSpot deal link to the MAP and capture the staging canary model request.

Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Reseed/checkpointing approach + rerank validation plan for Brightline migration

Hi Alyssa — quick answers inline and a couple new attachments (SOC2 summary + small ops checklist).

- PII: seed_manifest_v1.csv contains a pii_exclude column; we will run your PII filter as a pre-processing step in your environment when you send the export. We will not export or copy any fields marked pii_exclude. If you prefer, we can provide a tiny lambda to run on export to guarantee removal.
- SOC2: attaching SOC2-summary-2024.pdf (short summary). Full attestation can be shared under an NDA if Procurement needs it.
- Canary env: Redwood can provision an ephemeral staging cluster in your VPC (requires an IP allowlist); I'll kick off the infra request once you ok the MAP.
- Maintenance window: we will schedule heavy writes 02:00–06:00 local with a cap on concurrency and an automatic throttle if API errors spike. We suggest the Jun 18–19 staging canary and Jun 20–22 controlled prod backfill window.
- Pinecone metadata: yes; we can map Brightline visibility tags to metadata fields and filter at query time. We'll add a short schema mapping to the runbook.

Next step: I will create the MAP doc and send a calendar invite for a 30-minute MAP alignment next week.

Onwards —
Camila

Attachments: SOC2-summary-2024.pdf (pdf), backfill-runbook.pdf (updated checklist)

- Staging canary window: Jun 18–19 (provision an ephemeral cluster in our VPC; we will share IP allowlist and temporary creds).
- Prod backfill window: Jun 20–22 with low-traffic writes 02:00–06:00. We ask Redwood to limit write concurrency during the first 12 hours.
- Pinecone metadata mapping: agreed — please add the mapping section to the runbook.
- MAP meeting: weekly sync starting Mon Jun 16, 10:00 PT (we will accept the invite).

Action items on Brightline: export sample dataset by Jun 13 EOD and share a secure staging bucket.

I’ll wait for the MAP invite and the ephemeral cluster request.

Best,
Alyssa
